v.en: O God, come to my assistance;

r.la: Et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.
r.en: And my mouth shall declare thy praise.

full.en: Come * Let us glorify the Lord.

la: Iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.

Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
en: Let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

v.en: Sing to the Lord, O ye his saints.

r.en: And give praise to the memory of his holiness.

text.la: Dóminus de cælo * prospéxit super fílios hóminum.
text.en: The Lord hath looked down from heaven * upon the children of men.

text.la: Qui operátur iustítiam * requiéscet in monte sancto tuo, Dómine.
text.en: He who worketh justice * may rest on thy holy mountain, O Lord.

text.la: Inclína, Dómine, * aurem tuam mihi, et exáudi verba mea.
text.en: O Lord, incline * thy ear to me, and hear my voice, my Lord.

text.la: Retríbuet mihi Dóminus * secúndum iustítiam meam.
text.en: The Lord will reward me * according to my justice.

text.la: Exáudiat te * Dóminus in die tribulatiónis. ‡
text.en: May the Lord hear * thee in the day of tribulation. ‡

text.la: Dómine, * in virtúte tua lætábitur rex. ‡
text.en: The king rejoices * in Thy strength, O Lord. ‡

text.la: Exaltábo te, * Dómine, quóniam suscepísti me. ‡
text.en: I will extol thee, * O Lord, for thou hast upheld me. ‡

text.la: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
text.en: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

text.la: Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
text.en: O Lord Jesus Christ, graciously hear the prayers of Thy servants, and have mercy upon us, Who livest and reignest with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, ever world without end.

benedictio.la: Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.
benedictio.en: May the Eternal Father bless us with an eternal blessing.

source.en: Lesson from the book of Job

text.la: 1 Addidit quoque Iob assúmens parábolam suam, et dixit: 2 Vivit Deus, qui ábstulit iudícium meum, et Omnípotens, qui ad amaritúdinem addúxit ánimam meam. 3 Quia, donec súperest hálitus in me, et spíritus Dei in náribus meis, 4 Non loquéntur lábia mea iniquitátem, nec lingua mea meditábitur mendácium. 5 Absit a me, ut iustos vos esse iúdicem; donec defíciam, non recédam ab innocéntia mea.
text.en: 1 Job also added, taking up his parable, and said: 2 As God liveth, who hath taken away my judgment, and the Almighty, who hath brought my soul to bitterness, 3 As long as breath remaineth in me, and the spirit of God in my nostrils, 4 My lips shall not speak iniquity, neither shall my tongue contrive lying. 5 God forbid that I should judge you to be just: till I die I will not depart from my innocence.

body.la: Versa est in luctum cíthara mea, et órganum meum in vocem fléntium:
body.en: My harp is turned to mourning, and my organ into the voice of them that weep.

refrain.la: Parce mihi, Dómine, nihil enim sunt dies mei.
refrain.en: Let me alone, O Lord, for my days are vanity.

verse.la: Cutis mea denigráta est super me, et ossa mea aruérunt.
verse.en: My skin is black upon me, and my bones are burned with heat.

benedictio.la: Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.
benedictio.en: May the Son, the Sole-begotten, mercifully bless and keep us.

text.la: 6 Iustificatiónem meam, quam cœpi tenére, non déseram; neque enim reprehéndit me cor meum in omni vita mea. 7 Sit ut ímpius inimícus meus, et adversárius meus quasi iníquus. 8 Quæ est enim spes hypócritæ, si aváre rápiat, et non líberet Deus ánimam eius? 9 Numquid Deus áudiet clamórem eius, cum vénerit super eum angústia? 10 Aut póterit in Omnipoténte delectári, et invocáre Deum omni témpore?
text.en: 6 My justification, which I have begun to hold, I will not forsake: for my heart doth not reprehend me in all my life. 7 Let my enemy be as the ungodly, and my adversary as the wicked one. 8 For what is the hope of the hypocrite if through covetousness he take by violence, and God deliver not his soul? 9 Will God hear his cry, when distress shall come upon him? 10 Or can he delight himself in the Almighty, and call upon God at all times?

body.la: Utinam appenderéntur peccáta mea, quibus iram mérui,
body.en: O that my sins, whereby I have deserved wrath;

refrain.la: Et calámitas, quam pátior, in statéra.
refrain.en: And the calamity whereunder I suffer, were laid in the balances together.

verse.la: Quasi aréna maris hæc grávior apparéret, unde et verba mea dolóre sunt plena.
verse.en: For now it would appear heavier than the sand of the sea, therefore also my words are full of sorrow.

benedictio.la: Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.
benedictio.en: May the grace of the Holy Spirit enlighten all our hearts and minds.

text.la: 11 Docébo vos per manum Dei quæ Omnípotens hábeat, nec abscóndam. 12 Ecce vos omnes nostis, et quid sine causa vana loquímini? 13 Hæc est pars hóminis ímpii apud Deum, et heréditas violentórum, quam ab Omnipoténte suscípient: 14 Si multiplicáti fúerint fílii eius, in gládio erunt, et nepótes eius non saturabúntur pane; 15 Qui réliqui fúerint ex eo sepeliéntur in intéritu, et víduæ illíus non plorábunt.
text.en: 11 I will teach you by the hand of God, what the Almighty hath, and I will not conceal it. 12 Behold you all know it, and why do you speak vain things without cause? 13 This is the portion of a wicked man with God, and the inheritance of the violent, which they shall receive of the Almighty. 14 If his sons be multiplied, they shall be for the sword, and his grandsons shall not be filled with bread. 15 They that shall remain of him, shall be buried in death, and his widows shall not weep.

body.la: Quare detraxístis sermónibus veritátis? ad increpándum verba compónitis et subvértere nitímini amícum vestrum:
body.en: Why do ye argue against the words of truth? Do ye imagine words to reprove me and strive to confound one that is your friend?

refrain.en: Nevertheless, finish that ye have in mind.

verse.la: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
verse.en: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

text.la: Reliqua omittuntur, nisi Laudes separandæ sint.
text.en: Skip the rest, unless praying Lauds separately.

text.la: Custódi, Dómine, quǽsumus, Ecclésiam tuam propitiatióne perpétua: et quia sine te lábitur humána mortálitas; tuis semper auxíliis et abstrahátur a nóxiis et ad salutária dirigátur.
text.en: Keep, we beseech thee, O Lord, thy Church with thy perpetual mercy, and because the frailty of man without thee cannot but fall, keep us ever by thy help from all things hurtful, and lead us to all things profitable to our salvation.

office.title: Feria Secunda infra Hebd XIV post Octavam Pentecostes II. Septembris
